claims.title: Classical zero-free region for the Riemann zeta function, regional logarithmic-derivative bound, and square-root exponential remainder for the smoothed prime sum
claims.hypotheses: Riemann zeta function ζ with its simple pole at s = 1, von Mangoldt function Λ and Euler’s constant γ; complex s ≠ 1 measured against log(|Im s| + 2); real y ≥ 2 for the smoothed prime sum S(y) = ∑_{1≤n≤⌊y⌋} Λ(n)(y/n − 1) and its normalized error G(y) = S(y) − y log y + (1 + γ)y; and the disk lemma of LZE-01 (radius r > 0, growth ratio M ≥ 1, zeros counted with multiplicity on radius r/3, remainder at most 72 log M/r on radius r/6).
claims.statement: There is c₀ > 0 such that ζ(s) ≠ 0 whenever s ≠ 1 and Re s ≥ 1 − c₀/log(|Im s| + 2). There are c₁ > 0 and a real C₁ such that |ζ′(s)/ζ(s) + 1/(s − 1)| ≤ C₁ (log(|Im s| + 2))² whenever s ≠ 1 and Re s ≥ 1 − c₁/log(|Im s| + 2). There are c > 0 and a real K such that |G(y)| ≤ K y exp(−c √(log y)) for every y ≥ 2. Along the way, with C ≥ 0 the constant in |ζ′(s)/ζ(s)| ≤ 1/(Re s − 1) + C for Re s > 1, every zero β + it of ζ with |t| ≥ max(3, exp(3C)) satisfies β < 1 − (1/200000)/log(|t| + 2).
definitions: smoothed prime sum S(x) = ∑_{1≤n≤⌊x⌋} Λ(n)(x/n − 1) and normalized error G(x) = S(x) − x log x + (1 + γ)x
Perron integrand F_y(w) = −(ζ′(w)/ζ(w)) y^w/(w(w − 1)), with S(y) = (1/2π) ∫_ℝ F_y(σ₀ + iu) du for y ≥ 1 and σ₀ > 1
counterclockwise boundary integral of g over [x₀, x₁] × [y₀, y₁]: ∫_{x₀}^{x₁} g(x + iy₀) dx − ∫_{x₀}^{x₁} g(x + iy₁) dx + i ∫_{y₀}^{y₁} g(x₁ + iy) dy − i ∫_{y₀}^{y₁} g(x₀ + iy) dy

claims.correspondence: The coefficientwise identity 3 + 4 cos θ + cos 2θ = 2(1 + cos θ)² and the disk lemma on radius 1/2 with M = (|t| + 2)^10 give 4/(σ − β) ≤ 37201 log(|t| + 2) at σ = 1 + (1/10000)/log(|t| + 2), hence the exponent 1/200000 above height max(3, exp(3C)); compactness below that height gives min(1/200000, c₂ log 2). The regional bound splits into three regimes with constant (1441 + 60/c₀) + (4 + 4C_R) + 4|C_S|, and the Perron integral shifted to 1 − c/log(T + 2) with T = exp(c√(log y)/4) leaves the double-pole residue y log y − (1 + γ)y.

claims.title: Twisted Möbius inverse bound, uniform right-of-one logarithmic derivative, and local zero sum with derivative-witnessed multiplicities at 11/10 + it
claims.hypotheses: Modulus q ≥ 1, Dirichlet character χ modulo q with L-function L(s, χ), D_χ(s) = −L′(s, χ)/L(s, χ) and σ = Re s; the right-of-one constant C_R ≥ 0 for ζ from DZF-01; for the local sum, χ nonprincipal, t real, and a growth constant C with |L(s, χ)| ≤ C q (1 + |s|) for every nonprincipal χ and Re s ≥ 1/2 (the partial-summation estimate of LZE-02), C₁ = max(C, 1); for the disk lemma, f complex differentiable on the closed disk of centre z₀ and radius r > 0 with f(z₀) ≠ 0, |f| ≤ M |f(z₀)| on that disk and M ≥ 1.
claims.statement: For every q ≥ 1, every χ modulo q and Re s > 1, |L(s, χ)|⁻¹ ≤ σ/(σ − 1) and |D_χ(s)| ≤ 1/(σ − 1) + C_R. The disk lemma of LZE-01 holds with multiplicities m(ρ) ≥ 1 that satisfy m(ρ) ≥ 2 when f′(ρ) = 0 and m(ρ) = 1 when f′(ρ) ≠ 0. With C₀ = 120(1 + log(22C₁)/log 2), for every q ≥ 1, nonprincipal χ and real t, the zeros of L(·, χ) in the closed disk of centre 11/10 + it and radius 1/5 form a finite set Z with multiplicities m(ρ) ≥ 1, m(ρ) ≥ 2 whenever L′(ρ, χ) = 0, and Re D_χ(σ + it) ≤ C₀ log(q(|t| + 2)) − ∑_{ρ∈Z} m(ρ) Re(1/(σ + it − ρ)) for every 1 < σ ≤ 6/5.
definitions: negative logarithmic derivative D_χ(s) = −L′(s, χ)/L(s, χ)
local zero set Z = {ρ : |ρ − (11/10 + it)| ≤ 1/5, L(ρ, χ) = 0} with multiplicities m(ρ) ∈ ℕ, m(ρ) ≥ 1
growth ratio M = 22 C₁ q (|t| + 2) on the closed disk of centre 11/10 + it and radius 3/5, with |L(11/10 + it, χ)| ≥ 1/11

claims.correspondence: L(s, χ) times the twisted Möbius series equals one and the twisted von Mangoldt series is dominated termwise by the zeta series, giving σ/(σ − 1) and the zeta constant C_R uniformly in q and χ. Near a listed zero, f = (w − ρ)^m k with k(ρ) ≠ 0, so f′(ρ) = k(ρ) when m = 1 and f′(ρ) = 0 when m ≥ 2. The disk of radius 3/5 about 11/10 + it lies in Re z ≥ 1/2, the centre value is at least 1/11, the growth ratio is 22C₁q(|t| + 2), and the remainder is 72 log M/(3/5) = 120 log M.
claims.review: Checked (11/10)/(1/10) = 11, 1 + 11/10 + 3/5 ≤ 4 so 1 + |z| ≤ 2(|t| + 2), the radii 3/5 ÷ 3 = 1/5 and 3/5 ÷ 6 = 1/10 covering 1 < σ ≤ 6/5, log M ≤ (1 + log(22C₁)/log 2) log(q(|t| + 2)) from log(22C₁) ≥ 0 and log(q(|t| + 2)) ≥ log 2, and the product-rule computation of f′(ρ) for m = 1 and m ≥ 2.

claims.title: Principal-character reduction, uniform principal logarithmic-derivative bound, 3–4–1 character positivity, and exclusion of nonreal and large-height real zeros near Re s = 1
claims.hypotheses: Modulus q ≥ 1 with principal character 1_q, Dirichlet characters χ, χ₁, χ₂ modulo q, D_χ(s) = −L′(s, χ)/L(s, χ), real σ > 1 and t; regions Re s ≥ 1 − c/log(q(|Im s| + 2)); the zeta region, regional bound, growth and reciprocal bounds of DZF-01 and the inverse, right-of-one and local zero-sum bounds of DZF-02 with constants C_R ≥ 0 and C₀.
claims.statement: If Re s > 0, s ≠ 1 and L(s, 1_q) = 0, then ζ(s) = 0. There is C_P with Re D_{1_q}(σ + it) ≤ Re(1/(σ − 1 + it)) + C_P log(q(|t| + 2)) for every q ≥ 1, real t and 1 < σ ≤ 2. For σ > 1: 0 ≤ 3 Re D_{1_q}(σ) + 4 Re D_χ(σ + it) + Re D_{χ²}(σ + 2it) for every χ and t; 0 ≤ Re D_{1_q}(σ) + Re D_χ(σ) when χ² = 1_q; and 0 ≤ Re D_{1_q}(σ) + Re D_{χ₁}(σ) + Re D_{χ₂}(σ) + Re D_{χ₁χ₂}(σ) when χ₁² = χ₂² = 1_q. There is c > 0 such that L(s, χ) ≠ 0 whenever χ² ≠ 1_q and Re s ≥ 1 − c/log(q(|Im s| + 2)). For every δ > 0 there is c > 0 such that L(s, χ) ≠ 0 whenever χ² = 1_q, χ ≠ 1_q, |Im s| ≥ δ/log(q(|Im s| + 2)) and Re s ≥ 1 − c/log(q(|Im s| + 2)).
definitions: Dirichlet region of width c > 0 at modulus q: Re s ≥ 1 − c/log(q(|Im s| + 2))
principal constant C_P = K_ζ + 1 with K_ζ = 840 + |C_ζ| log 4 + |K₃|, where C_ζ is the regional constant for ζ and K₃ = ∑_n Λ(n) n^{−6/5}
nonreal exclusion constants A = 6|C₀| + 5C_R + 1, δ = min(1/10, 1/(2A)), c = δ/8; large-height constants K = 4 max(C₀, 0) + 2 max(C_P, 0) + 6C_R, a = min(δ/2, 1/10, 1/(4K + 1)), c = a/8

outstanding: The same-character small-height argument, the comparison of two real characters and the final assembly of the Dirichlet region with at most one exceptional zero are given in the exceptional-twist passages, which cite these three results as dependencies. Siegel’s lower bound for L(1, χ) is used by neither of the three results here.
